A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NOVA study. All 19 pages of v1 and 20 pages of v3, including equations, figures, tables and appendices, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original instruction-tuning experiments, benchmark results, ablations, parameter studies and human evaluation, including supplementary results in Appendices C–F.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds a qualitative analysis of ranked instruction samples in Appendix G.

M1.justification: ICP, NLI-based semantic clustering and voting, the quality reward model, equal-weight rank aggregation and subsequent instruction tuning are retained. The argument correction in Equation (9) matches the procedure already described in v1.

E1.justification: Training corpora and evaluation coverage are retained, including Alpaca, Alpaca-GPT4, BioGEN, LongFact, FollowRAG, MT-Bench and the UltraFeedback reward-model assessment. Appendix G examines existing Alpaca samples. The new mention of Chinese responses describes the existing test set.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain Vanilla tuning, FLAME-DPO-fact, SELF-EVAL, IFD, CaR and Nuggets. Appendix comparisons also retain the same NLI models, GPT comparators and method variants. Revised baseline descriptions do not establish changed implementations.

E3.justification: Appendix G introduces a small qualitative inspection procedure: compare the first- and last-ranked Alpaca samples under familiarity-only and final combined rankings. Existing benchmark settings, training budgets, selection ratios, model configurations and human-evaluation procedures are unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix G and Figure 8 examine how familiarity-only and combined rankings select different instruction samples. This supplements the existing generated-response case study in Table 4. Earlier ablations, sensitivity studies and design analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged. v3 introduces no repeated-run or seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Section 4.2 corrects the reported LongFact improvement range from 2.0–4.5% to 2.0–5.1%. Table 1 already reports 82.6 for Vanilla and 87.7 for NOVA-5% on Alpaca-GPT4 in both versions. Existing numerical results are unchanged; Figure 8 adds qualitative ranking outcomes.

T1.justification: Equation (9) corrects the displayed familiarity-score definition from F_res(q)/F_ins(r) to F_res(r)/F_ins(q), resolving inconsistent function arguments. The Gaussian assumption, entropy derivation, semantic-equivalence definitions and rank aggregation are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contribution: selecting familiar, high-quality instruction data through ICP, SEI and quality assessment reduces hallucinations while preserving instruction-following ability. Wording changes do not materially alter this claim.

C2.justification: Appendix G interprets ranking extremes as favoring simple, straightforward instructions under familiarity alone and associating low ranks with open-ended or subjective examples. It illustrates how quality assessment changes selection. Existing limitations concerning offline generation cost and single-turn filtering remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix E newly explains that the existing 100-instruction UltraFeedback test set is mostly English, with some translation tasks containing Chinese responses. This clarifies test composition. Hyperparameters, hardware, reward-model training details and the stated code/data availability remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds Si et al. (2025) on contextual faithfulness and removes the generic data-importance sentence and associated references, including Van Engelen and Hoos (2020) and Song et al. (2022). Positioning against quality-focused filtering and post-tuning reinforcement learning remains intact.

P1.justification: The abstract, introductory explanation, method descriptions and conclusion receive localized rewrites. v3 adds correspondence information, acknowledgements and Appendix G, while retaining the overall narrative and section organization.

P2.justification: v3 adds Figure 8, a four-example case-study panel, and makes small positioning and size adjustments to existing figures, including Figures 2 and 4. Existing tables and their organization are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 improves precision by correcting Equation (9) and making the LongFact summary agree with Table 1. The test-set clarification and ranking examples modestly improve transparency and explanation. Quantitative support remains unchanged. Appendix G introduces a wording inconsistency about 'familiar knowledge' promoting hallucinations, but this localized problem does not outweigh the limited gains.
